newsitem.title: USA: IBM to acquire Edmark for $80 mln.
newsitem.headline: IBM to acquire Edmark for $80 mln.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp and Edmark Corp said on Wednesday that they have agreed to merge for about $80 million in cash.
IBM will shortly commence a cash tender offer for shares of Redmond, Wash.-based Edmark at $15.50 per share, it said.
IBM expects to file documents with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 19, it said.
The conditions of the merger will include the acquisition of at least two-thirds of all outstanding shares of Edmark common stock on a fully diluted basis, it added.

"The merger of Edmark represents the next stage in our strategy of focusing on education and enhanced learning and further strengthens our leadership position in the home consumer marketplace," Jim Firestone, general manager of the IBM consumer division, said in a statement.
Edmark is a developer and publisher of consumer and educational software. IBM said it plans to operate the unit under the Edmark name in Redmond, with Firestone overseeing and directing operations.
"The merger brings to IBM a library of high quality educational software titles, as well as a highly experienced management and software development team," the companies said.
Edmark is the creator of the newly released Mighty Math Series, Sammy's Science House, Stanley's Stickers Stories, and the Thinkin' Things series.
